release.notes:
Accumulated release since 1.37.1: the `/ashlr-selftest` command, self-tuning compression, the companion handshake and doctor probes, lazy MCP tool loading, and reliability fixes for `brief-eval`, hook timing and macOS child-process waits.

### Added

- `/ashlr-selftest` (`scripts/selftest.ts`, also `ashlr-plugin selftest`): runs every command's entry point against a throwaway fixture repo with `--json` and reports pass/fail per command. Builds a temp git repo + isolated `$HOME`, probes every `/ashlr-*` command's backing script, every `ashlr-plugin` subcommand, and the real MCP stdio path (tools/list + `ashlr__read`/`ashlr__savings` calls). Pro-gated commands count their designed refusal as a pass; agent-only commands are listed as skipped; any `commands/*.md` file without a declared probe is reported as `uncovered` and fails the run. `--json` prints an `ashlr.selftest` v1 report; `--only`, `--keep-tmp` and `--timeout-ms` are supported.
- `scripts/brief-eval.ts --json` prints the eval report as JSON on stdout.
- Self-tuning compression, on by default (`ASHLR_TUNING=off` to disable): ashlr tracks per repo when a compressed `ashlr__read` or `ashlr__grep` result is followed by a native re-read of the same target, and adjusts `ashlr__grep` detail per extension within bounds (level -2 to +2, 20-sample minimum, one step per 20 results). Level 0 output is unchanged. `/ashlr savings` adds, per repo and UTC week, tokens saved, estimated re-read cost, net tokens saved (est.) and miss rate; per-repo savings are recorded in `~/.ashlr/repo-savings/` next to the unchanged global stats. State is local counts only under `~/.ashlr/{miss-stats,tuning,repo-savings}/`, capped and owner-only. See `docs/self-tuning.md`.
- `ashlr doctor --json` (`scripts/doctor.ts --json`) carries the shared `ashlr.doctor` v1 wrapper (`kind`, `schema_version`, `tool`, `status`, `native_status`, `checks`): failures are fail, else warnings are warn; `checks` flatten the section lines. Additive: every existing field and the exit code are unchanged. The vendored handshake contract and checker are re-vendored from ashlr-stack with the `doctor` section.
- Handshake conformance test (`__tests__/handshake-conformance.test.ts`): validates `ashlr-plugin --ashlr-handshake --json` and every health combination against the Ashlr handshake v1 contract vendored from ashlr-stack (`__tests__/contract/`, pinned by sha256). The plugin advertises no gated capability, so no doctor argv is run.
- `ashlr doctor` companions: a degraded lexicon or ashlr-md that lists the `doctor-fix` handshake capability gets the hint `run lexicon doctor --fix` or `run mdopener-mcp doctor --fix`, the same capability-only rule locus already had. Probes still run with no secrets in the environment.
- `ashlr doctor` companions: a degraded locus that lists the `doctor-fix` handshake capability gets the hint `run locus doctor --fix` (same rule as `stack doctor --ecosystem`). Lines show the reported health, a timeout or unreadable handshake reads as `unknown` instead of `outdated`, and `--json` adds `health` and `next_steps` to each companion.
- `ashlr doctor` has a **companions** section: phantom, phantom-secrets, locus, lexicon, ashlr-md and ashlr-stack are probed with `--ashlr-handshake --json` (2s timeout, no secrets in the env) and shown with version, readiness and a one-line fix hint when missing, outdated or degraded. Informational only; never a warning or failure. `scripts/doctor.ts --json` prints the report as JSON with a `companions` array.
- `ashlr-plugin --ashlr-handshake` prints the Ashlr companion handshake v1 (name, version, protocols, capabilities, local health, files the plugin may edit) as one JSON line. Answered by the node launcher before the bun check, so it works without bun. Contract: docs/ashlr-handshake.md.
- Deterministic lane-side merge-conflict resolution: `.gitattributes` gives `CHANGELOG.md` git's `merge=union` driver, and `bun scripts/resolve-mr-conflicts.ts` resolves stopped conflicts with no model call ; `CHANGELOG.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `README.md` keep the onto-branch version with the PR's hunks re-applied via union merge, while `bun.lock`, `package-lock.json` and `Cargo.lock` are regenerated by the package manager (frozen/locked mode first) rather than hand-merged. `__tests__/resolve-mr-conflicts.test.ts` rebases a fixture conflict end to end.

### Changed

- Per-repo savings use locked, atomic writes, with bounded retries even for malformed lock paths. The self-tuning report shows `n/a` net tokens when re-reads have no recorded savings.
- The savings dashboard abbreviates the stats path in its empty state, keeping long home directories within its 80-column layout. First-run Bun installation is detected using the updated PATH under Bun as well as Node.
- Hook timing batches count each row's bytes once before joining, avoiding repeated scans of growing batches that delay the hook safety timeout.
- The MCP router answers `initialize` and `tools/list` from `servers/_tool-catalog.json`, generated by `bun run gen:tool-catalog`. Each tool module is loaded on the first `tools/call` for that tool. Tool names, descriptions, input schemas, and call results are unchanged.

### Removed

- `scripts/prune-old-memories.ts` and `scripts/context-db-migrate.ts`: no command, hook, skill, doc or workflow invoked them. If you ran either by hand: the context database already migrates itself when a server opens it (`openContextDb`), and stale auto-memory files can be reviewed and deleted directly under your Claude projects `memory/` directory.

### Fixed

- `scripts/brief-eval.ts` no longer crashes on unrelated flags: `--level`/`--out` lookups previously read `args[0]` whenever the flag was absent, so `brief-eval.ts --json` threw `TypeError` (and `--out` could write a file literally named after the first argument). An invalid `--level` now exits 2 with a clear message.
- CI documentation drift: the README CI badge queried the removed `push` trigger (never rendered a status), and `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/platform-support.md`, `docs/launch-post.md`, `docs/producthunt.md` and `docs/press-kit/founder-bio.md` still described the pre-restructure model ; platform legs on every push, a weekly schedule and `ci:full-os` labels. All now describe the current model: PRs and merge-queue entries run only the seconds-fast `fast` gate; the full Linux/macOS/Windows suite and benchmark run on the daily schedule and `workflow_dispatch`. `__tests__/ci-docs.test.ts` pins the badge event parameter to a real workflow trigger and the documented cadence to the cron expression.
- `runWithTimeout` (`servers/_run-with-timeout.ts`) no longer loses a finished child on macOS under bun, where the runtime can drop `exit` and `close` forever while the child sits as a zombie (oven-sh/bun#34069); the happy-path `echo` test flaked this way on loaded CI runners. On POSIX the command now runs under a thin `/bin/sh` wrapper that reports its real exit status on a stderr trailer, so runs settle quickly with the true code even when process events never arrive. Missing and non-executable commands still return `exitCode: -1`, resolved the way execvp would before spawning. `warmUpSpawn` warms with the same spawn shape (detached, piped stdio) and retries inside its budget until an event is observed.

install.claude:
curl -fsSL https://plugin.ashlr.ai/install.sh | bash
/plugin marketplace add ashlrai/ashlr-plugin
/plugin install ashlr@ashlr-marketplace
/reload-plugins
install.codex:
codex plugin marketplace add ashlrai/ashlr-plugin
codex plugin add ashlr@ashlr-marketplace
ashlr-plugin codex-doctor --json
install.goose:
npm install -g ashlr-plugin
ashlr-plugin tools --json
cat > ashlr-goose.yaml <<'EOF'
version: "1.0"
title: ashlr token-efficiency suite
description: Registers the ashlr MCP router as one Goose extension.
extensions:
  - name: ashlr
    type: stdio
    cmd: ashlr-mcp
    args: []
    env:
      ASHLR_MCP_HOST: generic
EOF
goose run --recipe ashlr-goose.yaml

tools.name: ashlr__glob
tools.description: Match file globs instead of native Glob. Honors .gitignore in git repos; groups large result sets by directory with counts and sample paths.

tools.name: ashlr__tree
tools.description: View project structure in one call with directory sizes, file counts and optional LOC. Honors .gitignore in git repos; skips common build and dependency directories otherwise.

tools.name: ashlr__ls
tools.description: Gitignore-aware directory listing. Compact columnar output with elision past maxEntries (default 80). Set bypassSummary:true to see all entries.

tools.name: ashlr__diff
tools.description: Review adaptive git diffs instead of Bash git diff. Accepts refs, staged, unstaged or working; compresses large patches. Use ashlr__diff_semantic for refactors and renames.

tools.name: ashlr__webfetch
tools.description: Fetch article text instead of WebFetch. Strips HTML navigation/scripts, elides JSON arrays and caps plain text; default cap 100 KB.

tools.name: ashlr__read
tools.description: Read files instead of native Read with compact head/tail or AST summaries. Pass bypassSummary:true to skip LLM summarization; snipCompact truncation still applies.

tools.name: ashlr__flush
tools.description: Flush all queued ashlr__edit writes to disk immediately and return a summary of what was committed. Use when you need to read a file you just edited, or at the end of a multi-edit sequence.

tools.name: ashlr__edit_structural
tools.description: Rename symbols or extract functions in TS/JS using ASTs instead of native Edit; avoids strings/comments. Supports cross-file rename and dryRun. Use ashlr__edit for literal edits.

tools.name: ashlr__rename_file
tools.description: Move a source file and update resolved project imports, including extension elision and directory indexes. Supports dryRun; refuses existing destinations and paths outside cwd.

tools.name: ashlr__search_replace_regex
tools.description: Apply bulk regex substitutions instead of native Edit; supports captures, flags and dryRun. Returns match counts. Use ashlr__edit for literals or ashlr__edit_structural for symbol renames.

tools.name: ashlr__websearch
tools.description: Search the web instead of WebSearch with domain deduplication and compact snippets. query is required; maxResults defaults to 5, summarize to true.

tools.name: ashlr__task_list
tools.description: List tasks instead of TaskList with compact id, status, subject and age columns. Filter by status or owner; limit defaults to 30.

tools.name: ashlr__task_get
tools.description: Fetch a task by taskId instead of TaskGet. Returns status, subject and a compact description with head/tail truncation above 2 KB.

tools.name: ashlr__notebook_edit
tools.description: Edit one Jupyter notebook cell instead of NotebookEdit. Returns the edited cell and neighbors, eliding unrelated cells. Accepts notebookPath, cellIndex, newSource and optional cellType.

tools.name: ashlr__pipe
tools.description: [EXPERIMENTAL] Executes model-authored JS code server-side ; off by default, enable with ASHLR_PIPE_ENABLE=1. Call ctx.{grep,read,ls,glob} with the wrapped ashlr__ tool args; only the return value enters context. Typical 80–95% token savings vs individual calls. ctx.bash requires the additional ASHLR_PIPE_ALLOW_BASH=1 flag. Example: `return await ctx.grep({pattern:'TODO',cwd:'my project'});` returns the grep tool's text output as a string, which may include status messages.

tools.name: ashlr__fleet_state
tools.description: Read fleet targets, holds, last 20 jobs and latest leader event, with ~/.ashlr-runs fallback. Reports unavailable sources; never reads environment or secret files. Read-only.

tools.name: ashlr__fleet_events
tools.description: Poll typed dispatch and job events with an opaque per-source cursor. Reads complete lines only; limit up to 200. Reports missing, unsafe or malformed sources without raw contents. Read-only.

tools.name: ashlr__fleet_intent
tools.description: Append a pending fleet pause/resume, kill, reassign or set-slot request; never executes it. Requires requested_by and reason plus action-specific lane/job_id/slots. No caller-selected paths.

tools.name: ashlr__fleet_session
tools.description: Read a fleet job by ID: latest metadata, metrics, live children, PR, worktree and last 150 log lines. Redacts token-like strings; reports missing or unsafe sources. Read-only; no paths.

tools.name: ashlr__fleet_act
tools.description: Audit fleet pause/resume, kill, reassign, slots or steer requests. Requires requested_by and reason. dry_run defaults true; false queues controller review. Kill includes live children; never executes.

tools.name: ashlr__fleet_snapshot
tools.description: Read fleet lanes, complete job upserts, PR links and latest leader event, with ~/.ashlr-runs fallback. Pass cursor for net changes and removed IDs. Reports source errors. Read-only; no paths.

tools.name: ashlr__fleet_direction
tools.description: Read project direction (default VISION.md) or propose changes with author/text. Proposals append only to DIRECTION-PROPOSED.md; never adopt direction or write VISION.md or MASON-INBOX.md.

tools.name: ashlr__fleet_lanes
tools.description: Read fleet lane targets, holds, job counts and source errors as JSON using fleet-steer lanes. Read-only; fixed ~/.ashlr/fleet root, no arguments or paths.

tools.name: ashlr__fleet_proposals
tools.description: Read the fleet steering proposal journal and skipped-record count as JSON using fleet-steer proposals. Read-only; fixed ~/.ashlr/fleet/steer-proposals.jsonl, no arguments or paths.

tools.name: ashlr__fleet_propose
tools.description: Propose fleet reassign or set-slots for controller review, requiring author and reason. Rejects duplicate pending proposals; only appends the steering journal, never applies changes.

tools.name: ashlr__fleet_browser
tools.description: Read paged browser frames, latest frame and URL for a validated fleet job ID. Pass cursor for polling; limit defaults to 100, maximum 200. Read-only; accepts a job ID, never a path.

tools.name: ashlr__fleet_resources
tools.description: Read fleet resource availability, cap headroom, slot targets, throughput and exhaustion estimates. Refreshes missing or stale (>60s) ledger via ashlr resources --json. No arguments or paths.

tools.name: ashlr__grep
tools.description: Search instead of native Grep. Uses genome sections, merged PRs and closed issues when available; otherwise ripgrep with LLM summarization for large results. Returns compact relevant chunks.

tools.name: ashlr__edit
tools.description: Replace one literal match instead of native Edit; returns a compact diff. Strict mode requires one match. Use ashlr__multi_edit for multiple files or ashlr__edit_structural for symbol renames.

tools.name: ashlr__write
tools.description: Write a file without echoing its contents. Existing files use ashlr__edit for compact full-file replacement; new files return path, byte count and hash.

tools.name: ashlr__http
tools.description: HTTP fetch with compressed output. Readable-extracts main content from HTML, pretty-prints + array-elides JSON, bounded byte cap. Refuses non-http/https schemes and private hosts by default.

tools.name: ashlr__logs
tools.description: Tail logs with severity and ISO timestamp filters; collapse repeated lines. Supports glob paths, JSON/logfmt levels and Python tracebacks. since skips lines without parseable timestamps.

tools.name: ashlr__sql
tools.description: Run SQLite or Postgres queries and return compact text results. Supports SELECT, DDL, DML, EXPLAIN and schema introspection in one call.

tools.name: ashlr__diff_semantic
tools.description: Summarize refactors instead of raw git diff with heuristic AST-aware rename, signature and formatting detection. Use instead of ashlr__diff for refactors; falls back to compact diff.

tools.name: ashlr__pr
tools.description: Fetch a GitHub PR as a compact review summary: header, reviews, unresolved comments and checks. Read-only; never approves, comments or merges.

tools.name: ashlr__issue
tools.description: Fetch a GitHub issue and return a compact header + body + comment list. In 'thread' mode, each comment is rendered with snipCompact on > 500 char bodies. Read-only.

tools.name: ashlr__pr_comment
tools.description: Post a comment on a GitHub PR. Pass pr:"current" to target the PR for the checked-out branch. Returns the new comment URL.

tools.name: ashlr__pr_approve
tools.description: Approve a GitHub PR with an optional review body. Refuses to approve your own PR. Pass pr:"current" to target the PR for the checked-out branch.

tools.name: ashlr__issue_create
tools.description: Create a new GitHub issue with title + body and optional labels/assignees. Returns the new issue number and URL.

tools.name: ashlr__issue_close
tools.description: Close a GitHub issue with an optional closing comment and reason (completed|not_planned).

tools.name: ashlr__genome_propose
tools.description: Queue an update to a named genome section for the next ashlr__genome_consolidate call. Record decisions, strategies and lessons so they persist across sessions.

tools.name: ashlr__genome_consolidate
tools.description: Merge queued genome proposals. Applies sequentially without a model or ASHLR_LLM_URL; with an LLM configured, merges conflicting proposals for the same section.

tools.name: ashlr__genome_status
tools.description: Show pending proposals and recent mutations for the current genome. Compact report suitable for inline context.

tools.name: ashlr__fleet_ghosts
tools.description: Read ghost slots, stalled jobs and reported versus live counts by lane from ~/.ashlr/fleet/runs. Read-only JSON; unknown liveness and missing sources remain explicit. No arguments or paths.

tools.name: ashlr__fleet_dirty_triage
tools.description: Rank DIRTY PRs as recut-worthy, superseded or stale with C1-C6 reasons. repos defaults to current repo; staleDays to 14. Read-only pinned Locus queries; reports partial errors and truncation.

tools.name: ashlr__multi_edit
tools.description: Apply edits across files atomically instead of separate Edit calls; rolls back on failure and returns one diff summary. Use ashlr__edit for one file or ashlr__edit_structural for symbol renames.

tools.name: ashlr__orient
tools.description: Answer how a project works in one call: scan tree, retrieve relevant files, then ask a local LLM for a compact synthesis and suggested next tool. Uses genome when available, else ripgrep. Read-only.

tools.name: ashlr__bash
tools.description: Run commands instead of native Bash for verbose output. Compresses stdout above 2 KB and summarizes common commands; stderr stays intact. Refuses catastrophic patterns; use ashlr__read for cat.

tools.name: ashlr__bash_start
tools.description: Start a background shell command and return its session ID. Poll with ashlr__bash_tail, kill with ashlr__bash_stop, enumerate with ashlr__bash_list. Use for watchers, tails and long builds.

tools.name: ashlr__bash_tail
tools.description: Read new stdout/stderr for a background session; compresses output above 2 KB. Set wait_ms to wait for output or process exit, bounded by that ceiling.

tools.name: ashlr__bash_stop
tools.description: Kill a background session by id. Sends SIGTERM (configurable) and escalates to SIGKILL after 2s if still alive.

tools.name: ashlr__bash_list
tools.description: List active background sessions: id | pid | started | cumulative bytes | command.

tools.name: ashlr__test
tools.description: Run bun test, vitest, jest, pytest, go test or a generic runner. Returns compact pass/fail/skip counts and failures with file, line, message and stack for efficient debugging.

tools.name: ashlr__savings
tools.description: Show estimated tokens and cost saved by ashlr tools in the current session and lifetime totals. Use instead of manually counting tool calls to measure ashlr efficiency.

tools.name: ashlr__ask
tools.description: Ask a natural-language question; deterministically routes to ashlr__read, ashlr__grep, ashlr__orient, ashlr__tree or ashlr__glob. Output starts with the chosen tool and reason; routing uses no LLM.

commands.name: ashlr-allow
commands.description: Auto-approve every ashlr MCP tool so Claude Code stops prompting in bypass-permissions mode.

commands.name: ashlr-benchmark
commands.description: Run the ashlr-plugin token-savings benchmark against the current project.

commands.name: ashlr-brief
commands.description: Toggle response-shortening (caveman-inspired, ashlr-flavored) with three intensity levels. Trims filler from Claude's prose to save 30–55% on output tokens while keeping code blocks, errors, and destructive-action confirmations in full grammar.

commands.name: ashlr-budget
commands.description: Set, check, or clear a session spend cap. Guards against runaway tool use in long sessions.

commands.name: ashlr-compact
commands.description: Identify stale tool results accumulating in the conversation history and surface a recompression plan.

commands.name: ashlr-dashboard
commands.description: Rich token-savings dashboard ; per-tool bar charts, 7d/30d sparklines, projected annual savings, and cost in dollars.

commands.name: ashlr-doctor
commands.description: Diagnose an ashlr-plugin install ; checks plugin path, version, MCP servers, hooks, stats, genome, and settings in under 10 seconds.

commands.name: ashlr-eco-mode
commands.description: Toggle eco mode ; aggressive token-saving behaviors that trade some response richness for lower session cost.

commands.name: ashlr-fleet
commands.description: Explain the Phantom fleet pane, local peers, and governed Claude model routing.

commands.name: ashlr-genome-init
commands.description: Initialize a `.ashlrcode/genome/` in the current project so ashlr__grep can route through genome RAG for ~-84% token savings.

commands.name: ashlr-genome-keygen
commands.description: Generate an X25519 keypair for team-cloud genome v2 encryption and register the public half with Ashlr. Run this once per machine before running /ashlr-genome-team-init. Safe to re-run ; a no-op when the machine's key is already registered.

commands.name: ashlr-genome-loop
commands.description: Inspect and control the automatic genome propose + consolidate loop (PostToolUse observer + SessionEnd consolidator).

commands.name: ashlr-genome-push
commands.description: Push the local .ashlrcode/genome/ to the team cloud. Safe to run any time; invoked automatically at SessionEnd after consolidation. No-op when the repo has no .cloud-id (i.e. team-genome not initialized) or when ASHLR_CLOUD_GENOME_DISABLE=1.

commands.name: ashlr-genome-rewrap
commands.description: Re-wrap the team-cloud genome DEK for every member with a current pubkey. Run this after a teammate rotates their keypair (/ashlr-genome-keygen --force) or joins the team and runs /ashlr-genome-keygen for the first time. Admin-only.

commands.name: ashlr-genome-team-init
commands.description: Initialize (or rewrap for new members of) a team-cloud genome for the current repo. One-time per repo by an admin; then teammates join via /ashlr-team-invite + /ashlr-genome-keygen + admin re-runs with --wrap-all.

commands.name: ashlr-handoff
commands.description: Generate a context-pack for the next session to resume cold.

commands.name: ashlr-help
commands.description: List every ashlr slash command with a one-line description, grouped by category.

commands.name: ashlr-hook-timings
commands.description: Show per-hook latency report (p50/p95/max) from hook-timings.jsonl.

commands.name: ashlr-leaderboard
commands.description: Opt in or out of the public ashlr savings leaderboard at plugin.ashlr.ai/community. Opt-in is OFF by default; when on, your GitHub handle and total tokens/$ saved are shown publicly (never your email). Requires a signed-in account that syncs stats (Pro/Team).

commands.name: ashlr-legend
commands.description: Decode every element of the ashlr status line (plain-text legend).

commands.name: ashlr-ollama-setup
commands.description: Diagnose and guide local Ollama install so `/ashlr-genome-init --summarize` works reliably. Recommends a fast 3B model and smoke-tests it.

commands.name: ashlr-orchestrate-status
commands.description: Inspect past /ashlr-orchestrate runs ; list recent runs or drill into a single graph by id.

commands.name: ashlr-orchestrate
commands.description: Distributed-orchestration MVP ; expand a goal into a task graph, preview the DAG, confirm, and run it (Pro / Team only).

commands.name: ashlr-parallelize
commands.description: Spawn N parallel sub-agents ; one per file ; each applying the same task instruction. Merges results into a unified report.

commands.name: ashlr-report-crash
commands.description: Upload a recent ashlr-plugin crash dump to the maintainer. Opt-in, already-redacted, one report per invocation. Gives the founder faster bug signal when something in the plugin threw.

commands.name: ashlr-resume
commands.description: Resume your last coding session ; shows what you were doing, which files were active, and suggested next steps.

commands.name: ashlr-savings
commands.description: Show estimated tokens and cost saved by the ashlr-plugin this session and lifetime.

commands.name: ashlr-selftest
commands.description: Run every ashlr command's entry point against a throwaway fixture repo with --json and report pass/fail per command.

commands.name: ashlr-settings
commands.description: View or change ashlr-plugin settings.

commands.name: ashlr-spawn
commands.description: Spawn a named delegation pattern as one or more sub-agents. Patterns defined in _spawn-patterns.json.

commands.name: ashlr-status
commands.description: Report the ashlr-plugin activation status and MCP server health.

commands.name: ashlr-team-invite
commands.description: Invite someone to your ashlr team by email. Sends a magic-link invite (admin role required).

commands.name: ashlr-tier
commands.description: Three-phase tiered delegation ; explore (haiku) → implement (sonnet) → integration-check (haiku). Routes each phase to the right model tier automatically.

commands.name: ashlr-tour
commands.description: 60-second guided walkthrough of the ashlr-plugin on the current project ; proves the value of the tools on real files.

commands.name: ashlr-update
commands.description: Update the ashlr-plugin to the latest version from its git remote.

workflowSkills.name: ashlr-brief
workflowSkills.description: Tunable response-shortening skill for Claude Code. Trims filler from prose to reduce output tokens 30–55% while preserving grammar and code fidelity. Three intensity levels (lite / standard / concise). Auto-clarity exceptions for security, destructive actions, errors, and code blocks.

workflowSkills.name: ashlr-codex-doctor
workflowSkills.description: Check Ashlr's Codex plugin packaging, MCP manifest, hooks, skills, and workspace allow-list. Use when Codex setup, plugin loading, or MCP registration looks wrong.

workflowSkills.name: ashlr-codex-efficient-tools
workflowSkills.description: Codex-native efficient tool workflow. Prefer Ashlr MCP read, grep, tree, bash, savings, and genome tools before native scans when they reduce context.

workflowSkills.name: ashlr-codex-genome-refresh
workflowSkills.description: Refresh or maintain Ashlr project genome state from Codex. Use after architectural changes, schema/routing changes, or substantial refactors.

workflowSkills.name: ashlr-codex-parallel-explore
workflowSkills.description: Efficient parallel exploration habits for Codex. Use when a task needs several independent codebase questions answered before implementation.

workflowSkills.name: ashlr-codex-savings
workflowSkills.description: Inspect Ashlr token savings from Codex using host-neutral CLI and MCP surfaces.

workflowSkills.name: ashlr-cost-refactor
workflowSkills.description: Token-efficient refactoring discipline for Claude Code. Diff-first before editing, structural edits for renames, find-all-refs then one multi_edit per file, no re-reads between edits, one genome proposal at the end. Reduces refactor session cost 40–65%.

workflowSkills.name: ashlr-efficient
workflowSkills.description: Output structure reshaper for Claude Code. Complements ashlr-brief's prose trimming by enforcing inverted-pyramid order, inline code for identifiers, tables for multi-item comparisons, and no transitional filler. Works standalone or alongside ashlr-brief.

workflowSkills.name: ashlr-genome-author
workflowSkills.description: Guidelines for when and how to call ashlr__genome_propose to keep the project genome accurate. Covers post-architectural-decision proposals, correct summary format, and what NOT to propose. Keeps the genome signal-rich without noise.

workflowSkills.name: ashlr-lean-tools
workflowSkills.description: Highest-impact token-saving habits for Claude Code tool use. Read-once, batch edits, orient-before-search, skip verification reads, grep-before-read, concise output at high spend. Reduces session token cost 30–60%.

workflowSkills.name: ashlr-search
workflowSkills.description: Genome-aware search habits for Claude Code. Prefer ashlr__grep and ashlr__glob over native scans; compose multi-term queries; trust genome summaries; orient once before searching. Reduces redundant reads and search token cost 40–70%.
